excerpt: For these experiments the authors use an execution count threshold of 100 before adding basic blocks to a trace. Table 6 reports profile-based executable size ratios relative to globally optimized programs: cccp 1.03, cmp 1.11, compress 1.01, eqn 1.10, eqntott 1.00, espresso 1.07, grep 1.09, lex 1.08, mpla 1.13, tbl 1.06, wc 1.01, xlisp 1.20, yacc 1.09, with average 1.07.
overview: This evidence addresses the main cost risk of super-block formation: tail duplication can increase code size. The reported threshold and size ratios show a deliberate control mechanism and quantify the remaining expansion. The worst listed case is larger than average, so the result supports controlled rather than zero-cost growth.
title: Code Expansion Ratios
